threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'thank you' to the bus driver. Locals just nod or look away, like it’s some unwritten rule.
Last night the 88 was packed, but the guy in the back was singing old Spice Girls tunes. Everyone joined in, even the driver chuckled.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw my Kiosk guy bribe a raccoon for his leftover döner. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a club featuring techno in a former bread factory. The scent of fresh bread mingling with bass is uniquely surreal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they instinctively check the BART schedule for delays before heading to a late match, even while sipping on a Mission burrito.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing chess on the 19 bus last night. He was talking strategies louder than the engine. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about the hipster cafes, but real locals still rely on the old-school fruit markets on Travessera.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always stop to take photos of the street art, but their expressions scream confusion when they can't find the nearest metro.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newbies when they say 'the tube' instead of 'the underground'. Also, who needs a jacket in the evening? It's a different climate here.
Caught a glimpse of a bloke in a full suit arguing with a street lamp at 2 AM. He was convinced it was his ex. Real Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting in the park, I watched a group of kids teach a stray dog to fetch sticks—only in Neukölln could chaos look so cozy.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst from a stand while listening to a spontaneous jam session in the park—it's like street food meets live music.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they roll their eyes when someone calls it 'Frisco'—it's either endearing or a dealbreaker.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I saw a guy in a tuxedo catch the 19 while balancing a bouquet of roses—classic San Francisco hustle wrapped in elegance.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always misjudge the siesta. It’s not just a nap, it’s when entire streets go silent, like the city is holding its breath.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand at the tram stop, checking their phones every two minutes like it's a life raft.
